items.title: 63520_Ernie Fields oral history interview
items.q: And then I'd go and rehearse, and I learned an awful lot from him.

ctx.x: T is still living, he's in his eighties. He's not too sharp but he remembers some of that and remembers me and he remembers how they would have these rehearsals and he wouldn't let anybody come in. He would have closed door rehearsals, where they came to the door and they would say Ernie Fields is here, he's got a little band, and he would say, let him in. And then I'd go and rehearse, and I learned an awful lot from him.

I remember one day that he was lecturing to his guys and he told them that I don't want to see what happened last night, and I think somebody says what? He said, so and so is playing a solo and made an error and said it just tickled you to death and everybody went looking around at each other. He said if you are not playing your horn and setting the rhythm for the soloist, if he does anything wrong, you better be grinning and clapping your hand like he played it right. And he said if
